metadata.case_name: CHIU TSZ YING v. HUI KA CHUN AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: tibial plateau fracture of the right knee
source: The Plaintiff was diagnosed to have suffered a tibial plateau fracture of the right knee, and right pubic rami, and abrasions to her left knee. She required admission to hospital on two occasions, the first for surgery immediately after the injury, in which she was hospitalised for 11 days, the second for the removal of an implant stabilising the knee, in which she was hospitalised for three days.

injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pubis without disruption of pelvic ring

source: The Plaintiff was diagnosed to have suffered a tibial plateau fracture of the right knee, and right pubic rami, and abrasions to her left knee. She required admission to hospital on two occasions, the first for surgery immediately after the injury, in which she was hospitalised for 11 days, the second for the removal of an implant stabilising the knee, in which she was hospitalised for three days.

The Plaintiff, aged 19 at the time of the accident, suffers right knee pain and stiffness. She has a 12°valgus deformity of the right leg, and five scars on the lateral aspect of her right knee. It is right that, anatomically, the femur and tibia in females normally forms a valgus angle of 4°to 8°, and the valgus angle of the Plaintiff’s left knee is 8°. However, contrary to the assertion of Dr Lam, that does not demonstrate a small deformity in the right knee, but a significant deformity, one of 4°. She has a 10°deflection deformity of her right knee, and her right knee movement is limited. Her orthopaedic surgeon has assessed total bodily impairment at 10%.
